title: Stitch removal
what: A doctor or nurse cuts and pulls out the threads or staples that closed your wound. It is usually quick and almost painless.
why: When the wound has healed enough. Most often after 5 to 14 days, depending on where the stitches are and what kind they are.
tell_doctor: If the wound is red, painful, or leaking
If you have diabetes or take steroid medicines. Healing may take longer

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Come on the day your doctor gave you. Do not remove them earlier, or the wound may open.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable, so the stitches are easy to uncover.

bring: Your hospital discharge papers or referral
steps: The dressing is removed and the stitches are checked
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
Tweezers lift the knot, and scissors cut the thread
The thread is pulled out, one for each stitch
Staples are removed with a special tool
The area is cleaned and covered with a plaster if needed
feel: A light tug or pinch as the thread comes out
after: Usually you can get the area wet 1 to 2 days after removal. Check with your doctor
Do not scrub the area or tan for a few months. This helps the scar fade
The scar is red at first, then slowly fades over months
red_flags: Redness, swelling, pus, or a fever

faq.a: Usually not. You feel a light tug. Numbing is usually not needed.
Better not. There is a risk of infection, and part of the thread may stay in the skin. A doctor or nurse should do it.

faq.q: After how many days are stitches removed?
faq.a: Usually after 5 to 7 days on the face, and 7 to 14 days on the body, arms, and legs. Your doctor will tell you the exact day.
